question: As we go down under water in a ocean the water pressure:

options.text: remains constant and equal to the atmospheric pressure

solution:
The correct answer is __**increases**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Force acting on a unit area is called pressure.
 
• The pressure increases with increasing depth.
 
• This is due to the water up above weighs down on the water below.
 
• Liquid pressure increases as depth increases.
 
• The pressure is greater on lower surfaces of the body than on the upper surfaces as the pressure in a fluid increases with depth.
 
• Pressure and depth are directly proportional to each other.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• The pressure at sea level is taken as the standard atmospheric pressure.
 
• As the height increases from sea level, the atmospheric pressure decreases.
 
• At high altitudes where atmospheric pressure is less, it bleeds from the nose due to high blood pressure.
 
• SI unit of pressure is the pascal.
